obligations.title: Risk Management System
obligations.description: Establish, document, implement, maintain and update a risk management system in relation to high-risk AI systems.
obligations.guidance: Document risk assessment methodology, identified risks and mitigation measures. Regular reviews required.

obligations.title: Data Governance and Quality Management
obligations.description: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be subject to data governance and management practices covering design choices, collection processes, preparation operations, assumptions, assessment of availability, quantity and suitability, examination for bias, and identification of gaps. Data sets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible free of errors and complete.
obligations.guidance: Document design choices, collection processes, preparation operations, assumptions, availability/quantity/suitability assessments, bias examination, and identified gaps. Ensure training, validation and testing data sets are relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible free of errors and complete.

obligations.title: Technical Documentation
obligations.description: Draw up technical documentation of the high-risk AI system before that system is placed on the market or put into service.
obligations.guidance: Comprehensive documentation as per Annex IV. Must cover system architecture, data, training, validation, documentation.

obligations.title: Record-Keeping
obligations.description: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system. Logging capabilities shall enable a level of traceability appropriate to the intended purpose of the system, covering (a) situations that may result in the AI system presenting a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1) or that may lead to a substantial modification, (b) facilitation of post-market monitoring referred to in Article 72, and (c) monitoring of the operation of the high-risk AI system referred to in Article 26(5).
obligations.guidance: Ensure the system can automatically record events (logs) over its lifetime with traceability appropriate to the intended purpose. Logs must support risk situations under Article 79(1) or substantial modification, post-market monitoring under Article 72, and operational monitoring under Article 26(5). Article 19 sets a six-month minimum retention period for automatically generated logs for providers.

obligations.title: Transparency and Provision of Information to Deployers
obligations.description: Provide deployers with all necessary information to use the high-risk AI system in compliance with this Regulation.
obligations.guidance: Provide clear instructions for use, expected level of accuracy, limitations, any human oversight measures.

obligations.title: Human Oversight
obligations.description: Design and develop high-risk AI systems in such a way that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which the AI system is in use.
obligations.guidance: Enable humans to detect automation bias, unexpected outputs, and intervene or interrupt the system.

obligations.title: Accuracy, Robustness and Cybersecurity
obligations.description: Design and develop high-risk AI systems in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity.
obligations.guidance: Implement measures to ensure accuracy, resilience to errors, resistance to cyber-attacks, and reliable output.

obligations.title: Quality Management System
obligations.description: Establish, implement, document and maintain a quality management system to ensure and demonstrate conformity with this Regulation.
obligations.guidance: ISO 9001-compliant QMS covering design, development, testing, validation, documentation and maintenance.

obligations.title: Conformity Assessment
obligations.description: Before placing on the market a high-risk AI system, the provider shall carry out the relevant conformity assessment procedure.
obligations.guidance: Perform self-assessment or third-party assessment as per Annex V/VI/IX. Affix CE marking if compliant.

obligations.title: Post-Market Monitoring by Providers
obligations.description: Establish and document a post-market monitoring system to keep monitoring the compliance of AI systems with this Regulation.
obligations.guidance: Continuously monitor system performance, collect and analyze relevant data, report serious incidents to authorities.

obligations.title: EU Database Registration
obligations.description: Before placing on the market or putting into service a high-risk AI system, the provider shall register the system in the EU database referred to in Article 71.
obligations.guidance: Register the AI system in the EU public database before market placement. Include provider identity, system description, intended purpose, risk level, conformity assessment status, and Member States where the system is placed on the market.

obligations.title: Human Oversight
obligations.description: Ensure that natural persons effectively oversee the high-risk AI system during the period in which the AI system is in use.
obligations.guidance: Assign competent human personnel to monitor system operation and intervene when necessary.

obligations.title: Data Quality and Governance
obligations.description: Use high-risk AI systems in such a way that appropriate data governance and management practices are applied.
obligations.guidance: Ensure relevant, sufficiently representative, accurate and complete input data for the system.

obligations.title: Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment
obligations.description: Before deploying a high-risk AI system, carry out a fundamental rights impact assessment (FRIA) to evaluate the impact on the rights of persons affected.
obligations.guidance: Conduct a FRIA covering: description of deployer's processes using the AI system, period and frequency of use, categories of affected persons, specific risks of harm, human oversight measures, and measures taken in case of materialization of risks. Notify the relevant market surveillance authority of the results.

obligations.title: Provide Information to Affected Persons
obligations.description: Inform natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system, unless the deployer does not have access to the information.
obligations.guidance: Inform affected natural persons of the use of the high-risk AI system (Article 26(11)). Where individual decision-making is involved, also consider the right to explanation under Article 86.

obligations.title: Chatbot Disclosure
obligations.description: Ensure that users are informed that they are interacting with an AI system unless this is obvious from the circumstances and the context of use.
obligations.guidance: Display clear indication that the interaction is with an AI system. Ensure disclosure is visible and understandable.

obligations.title: Deepfake Disclosure
obligations.description: Label artificially generated or manipulated image, audio or video content as such.
obligations.guidance: Clearly mark AI-generated content. Include metadata where technically feasible. Exception for authorized law enforcement.

obligations.title: Emotion Recognition Disclosure
obligations.description: Inform natural persons that they are subject to emotion recognition systems unless this is obvious from the circumstances.
obligations.guidance: Notify individuals when emotion recognition is being used. Obtain consent where required by data protection law.

obligations.title: General Transparency Obligations
obligations.description: Comply with transparency obligations when deploying limited-risk AI systems subject to this Article.
obligations.guidance: Ensure AI system interactions are clearly identified. Provide adequate information to users about system capabilities and limitations.
